items.title: Nat Hentoff interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: Bill Clinton reluctantly went into Kosovo to stop those mass murders.

ctx.x: He predicted that the Republicans were going to really like go down the tubes election- wise. But it was pre-Bush.

Yeah, unless he was really a prophet I don’t think he could have realized the terrible lack of understanding of what we were going into on the part of the people like Rumsfeld, like Bush, like Dick Cheney, who is really, he’s really the president. I don’t mean this in some kind of tabloid sense. There’s a very good documentary series that comes out of WGBH, it’s on PBS, it’s called “Frontline.” And I’ve done a lot of research on this. But a week or two ago when we were doing this interview, they had an hour, with…
Wow. Do you think the democrats will be able to make some kind of difference?

items.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I almost got him into trouble during the Clinton years, because Clinton’s lawyer was – lawyers were at Williams and Connolly, and I was then writing for the Washington Post.

ctx.x: She’s a pianist [and] singer. Hasn’t done much club work lately, because she has a kid. She spends – she makes her living primarily as a piano teacher. In some circles in New York I’m known as Mandy’s father, because she’s taught their kids. And she writes for television. She’s written for “Front Line” and other documentaries. The boys – the first son is Nick – Nick Hentoff. He’s a lawyer who takes cases that very few other lawyers would take. He’s based in Arizona. He does criminal defense work, civil liberties…
Are they both – are the two – are the four children from the same marriage?
